title: The Mode: Most Popular Wins
objective: After this level you can find the mode and explain when the most common value is the most useful average, as with shoe sizes.
summary: The mode is the most common value. It is the only average that works for categories like colors, and it suits questions like which shoe size to stock.

cards.headline: A shoe shop doesn't want the average size. It wants the size people buy.
cards.body: Stocking up on the mean would be a strange plan. The shop needs a third kind of average: the one that simply counts which value turns up most.

cards.headline: The most common value
cards.body: The mode is the value that appears most often. Say five customers wear sizes 6, 7, 7, 7 and 11. The mode is 7: three of the five wear it. The mean is 38 ÷ 5 = 7.6, a size nobody in the group wears. For deciding which boxes to order, the mode is the average that fits.

cards.headline: The only average for words
cards.body: Ask a class for favorite colors: red, red, red, green, green, yellow, purple, black, blue. You cannot add colors, and you cannot line them up from small to large, so there is no mean and no median. But you can count them, and red wins. Of the three averages, only the mode works for categories like colors.

cards.fact: A set can have two modes, or none at all.
cards.context: If two values tie for most common, the set is bimodal. If every value is different, there is no mode. And the most common value is not always central: in Level 12's 11 retirement ages, the mode is 54, while the middle is 57.

cards.headline: The mode: most common
learned: The mode is the most common value

questions.prompt: What is the mode of a set of values?

options.label: The value halfway between the smallest and largest
options.rationale: That is a midpoint, not the mode.

options.label: The value that appears most often
The middle value once they are in order

questions.explanation: The mode is the most common value: size 7, worn by three of the five customers.

questions.prompt: A café's customers order tea, coffee, coffee, juice, coffee and tea. Which average can describe the orders?

options.label: The mean, because it counts every order
The median, the order in the middle
options.rationale: Drinks cannot be lined up from small to large.

questions.explanation: Drinks are categories: you cannot add them or order them, but you can count them. Coffee is the most common.

questions.prompt: For shoe sizes 6, 7, 7, 7 and 11, why does a shop prefer the mode to Level 11's mean?

options.label: The mean, 7.6, is a size nobody in the group wears
The mean is always larger than the mode
options.rationale: Not always; here the size 11 pulls it up.

options.label: The mode uses every value in the list
options.rationale: The mean uses every value; the mode just counts.

options.label: A mean cannot be worked out for shoe sizes

questions.explanation: The mean shares the total (38) out over five people to get 7.6, which fits nobody; the mode, 7, is what most people wear.
